title: Christa Pike Survives Failed Execution, Now Awake and Speaking
title_zh: 死刑执行失败后，克里斯塔·派克苏醒并能说话了
lead: A death row inmate in Tennessee has reportedly survived a lethal injection and regained consciousness, a scenario her lawyers call medically unprecedented. As authorities remain silent on what went wrong, the case raises profound questions about capital punishment.
lead_zh: 田纳西州一名死囚据称在注射死刑失败后幸存并恢复意识，她的律师称这种情况在医学上史无前例。当局对失败原因保持沉默，此案引发了对死刑执行的深刻质疑。
preview: Christa Pike, a 50-year-old death row inmate in Tennessee, is "conscious and speaking" after surviving a failed execution attempt last week,
preview_zh: 田纳西州50岁的死囚克里斯塔·派克上周在一次失败的处决后幸存，她的律师周二表示，她目前“意识清醒并能说话”。她仍被铐在医院，接受重症医疗护理。派克因1995年谋杀科琳·斯莱默被判处死刑。上周三，她经历两次失败的注射死刑后住院，昏迷数日，医疗人员一直在清除她体内的注射药物。
paragraphs: Christa Pike, a 50-year-old death row inmate in Tennessee, is "conscious and speaking" after surviving a failed execution attempt last week, her attorneys said on Tuesday. She remains handcuffed in hospital, receiving critical medical care. Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer. Last Wednesday, she survived two failed lethal injections and was subsequently hospitalised, remaining unconscious for days as medical staff cleared the injected chemical from her body.

Experts and her legal team describe her apparent recovery as unprecedented. She is believed to be the only person ever to survive a lethal injection. Her lawyers called her progress "medically unprecedented," cautioning that while her prognosis remains unclear, "at a minimum, we expect a long recovery." Deborah Denno, a criminologist at Fordham Law School, said she was "absolutely astonished" that Pike is conscious and speaking.

Denno noted that in seven other cases where prisoners survived scheduled executions, executioners were unable to inject anything into their veins. Pike, however, "is the only person for whom some kind of toxin has been injected," she said. "They did everything they were supposed to do as part of the execution process, and it simply didn't work. This has never happened before." Authorities have not said whether they will try again to execute Pike, nor have they explained what went wrong after injecting her with the chemical pentobarbital.

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee suspended all executions for the rest of the year, and the state's prisons chief said over the weekend that he plans to resign. Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for troubled teens. Pike's attorneys are scheduled to appear in court in Nashville on Wednesday and plan to hold a news conference outside the court.

Dr Joel Zivot, an anaesthesiologist advising Pike's defence team, said on Tuesday that the likelihood of recovering from lethal injection is low. "Most people who get lethal injection die from it," he told the BBC. "In fact, pretty well everyone, except Christa. So, the fact that she survived it ... was unusual." But he stressed that many unknowns remain, including how much pentobarbital entered her system and what her recovery will look like. "I would not, in any way, say at this point that all the big risks are behind her," he noted.

Zivot had previously said the two doses of pentobarbital she received would have been enough that, had it entered her bloodstream in normal circulation, "she would have surely died." Instead, he suggested the drug likely spread across the tissue under her skin rather than entering her bloodstream. He thought a brain injury was "very possible" due to delays in resuscitating her, and believed it would take about a week to truly understand her condition. It has now been six days since the failed attempt.
paragraphs_zh: 田纳西州50岁的死囚克里斯塔·派克上周在一次失败的处决后幸存，她的律师周二表示，她目前“意识清醒并能说话”。她仍被铐在医院，接受重症医疗护理。派克因1995年谋杀科琳·斯莱默被判处死刑。上周三，她经历两次失败的注射死刑后住院，昏迷数日，医疗人员一直在清除她体内的注射药物。
专家及其法律团队称她的明显康复是史无前例的。据信，她是唯一一个在注射死刑后幸存的人。她的律师称她的进展“在医学上史无前例”，并警告说，虽然预后尚不清楚，“但至少，我们预计需要长期康复”。福德汉姆法学院的犯罪学家黛博拉·丹诺表示，她对派克能清醒说话感到“绝对震惊”。
丹诺指出，在其他七起死囚幸存案例中，行刑者未能将药物注入囚犯静脉。而派克“是唯一被注射了某种毒素的人”，她说。“他们按照处决程序做了所有该做的事，但就是没起作用。这种情况从未发生过。”当局尚未说明是否会再次尝试处决派克，也未解释注射戊巴比妥后出了什么问题。
田纳西州州长比尔·李暂停了今年剩余时间的所有处决，该州监狱负责人周末表示计划辞职。派克18岁时和当时的男友塔达里尔·希普一起殴打、折磨并杀害了19岁的斯莱默，他们是在一个为问题青少年举办的职业培训营认识的。派克的律师定于周三在纳什维尔出庭，并计划在法院外举行新闻发布会。
派克辩护团队的麻醉师顾问乔尔·齐沃特博士周二表示，从注射死刑中恢复的可能性很低。“大多数人被注射死刑后都会死亡，”他告诉BBC。“事实上，除了克里斯塔，几乎所有人都是如此。所以，她能活下来……很不寻常。”但他强调，仍有许多未知因素，包括有多少戊巴比妥进入了她的体内，以及她的康复情况会如何。“我现在绝不会说，所有重大风险都已经过去了，”他指出。
齐沃特此前曾表示，她上周接受的两剂戊巴比妥，如果通过正常循环进入血液，足以“让她必死无疑”。相反，他提出一种可能的解释：药物可能没有进入派克的血液，而是扩散到了她皮肤下的组织。他认为，由于复苏延迟，她“很可能”出现脑损伤，并认为大约需要一周才能真正了解她的状况并进行神经系统检查。现在距离那次失败的处决已经六天了。

title_original: US death row inmate Christa Pike awake and speaking after failed execution, lawyers say
summary_original: Experts and lawyers called the apparent recovery unprecedented, noting she is believed to be the only known person to survive a lethal injection.
body_original:
US death row inmate Christa Pike awake and speaking after failed execution, lawyers say
By
Sareen Habeshian
and
Kwasi Gyamfi Asiedu
Published
6 October 2026
Updated 57 minutes ago
US death row inmate Christa Pike is "conscious and speaking" after surviving a failed execution attempt last week, her lawyers say.
Pike, 50, continues to receive critical medical care while handcuffed in hospital, her attorneys said in a statement on Tuesday.
Pike, who was sentenced to death after murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995, survived two failed lethal injections last Wednesday in Tennessee. She was taken to hospital, where she remained unconscious for days as medical staff cleared her body of the injected chemical.
Experts and her legal team say her apparent recovery is unprecedented. She is believed to be the only person to survive a lethal injection.
Her lawyers called her progress "medically unprecedented", and while her prognosis remains unclear, "at a minimum, we expect a long recovery".
Deborah Denno, a criminologist and professor at Fordham Law School, said she was "absolutely astonished" that Pike is conscious and speaking.
There were seven other cases where prisoners survived slated executions, but in those cases, executioners were not able to inject anything into the inmates' veins, Denno told the BBC.
Pike "is the only person for whom some kind of toxin has been injected," she said.
"They did everything they were supposed to do as part of the execution process, and it simply didn't work," Denno said. "This has never happened before."
Authorities have not yet said whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have also not offered an explanation for what went wrong after injecting her with the chemical pentobarbital.
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee suspended all executions for the rest of the year - and the head of prisons in the state said over the weekend that he plans to resign.
Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for troubled teens.
Pike's attorneys are scheduled to appear in court in Nashville on Wednesday. They also plan to hold a news conference outside the court.
Dr Joel Zivot, an anaesthesiologist advising Pike's defence team, said on Tuesday that the likelihood of recovering from lethal injection is low.
"Most people who get lethal injection die from it," he told the BBC. "In fact, pretty well everyone, except Christa. So, the fact that she survived it ... was unusual."
But there remains a lot of uncertainty and many unknowns, he said, including how much of the pentobarbital got into her system, what her blood levels were after the injection and what her recovery will look like.
"I would not, in any way, say at this point that all the big risks are behind her," he noted.
Zivot had previously said the two doses of pentobarbital she received last week would have been enough that, had it entered her bloodstream in normal circulation, "she would have surely died".
Instead, Zivot said a possible explanation is that instead of entering Pike's bloodstream, the pentobarbital was more likely to have spread across the tissue under her skin.
Zivot said last week he thought her ending up with a brain injury was "very possible", due to the delays in resuscitating her. He also believed it would take about a week to truly understand her condition and do a neurological exam. It's now been six days since the failed attempt to execute her.
Pike's lawyers previously warned that her medical history and anatomy - including thrombocytosis (a blood-clotting condition) and small veins - meant there was a risk she would experience "unnecessary" pain and suffering during a lethal injection.
They said on Tuesday that she has endured "severe damage" to her arms.
